answer: Admission is capped at 3 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. A farm hence spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the sonnet quota and the knoll admission check. Because the quartz audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 3 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
